summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a complex medical history including Crohn’s disease, short bowel syndrome, SVC syndrome, and prior port infections was readmitted for recurrent fevers and severe back and groin pain shortly after completing a two-week course of IV vancomycin for Bacillus cereus bacteremia. She presented with vomiting, tachycardia, and pain unresponsive to oral opioids. Workup revealed a urinary tract infection with Klebsiella, prompting treatment with ciprofloxacin. MRI showed significant improvement in the right pectineus muscle abscess, now reduced to a 3 mm fluid focus. A transesophageal echocardiogram ruled out endocarditis. Due to persistent inflammation and clinical concern, infectious disease recommended completing an additional two-week course of IV vancomycin. Her pain was managed with IV dilaudid and benadryl, and urinary retention resolved. An incidental enchondroma in the right femur was noted and recommended for outpatient follow-up. She remained afebrile for 24 hours prior to discharge, was hemodynamically stable, and transitioned to home IV antibiotics with a structured pain taper and updated warfarin dosing. Outpatient follow-up was arranged for labs, imaging, and hematology recheck.
